caption:
Nobody rewatches a video because it was good. They rewatch it because it was about them.

Here's what Instagram actually counts: watch time on a reel includes replays. One person, 30 seconds, watched twice = 60 seconds of watch time on 30 seconds of content. Mosseri named watch time and sends per reach as two of the three signals that decide reach.

So the question was never "how do I make this better." It's "how do I make them watch it again."

The move:
1. Find the thing your audience quietly feels bad about.
2. Say it out loud.
3. Flip it into a strength.

"You're not bad at marketing. You're too busy doing the actual work."

That line doesn't feel like selling. It feels like being seen. So they watch it again — and they send it to the one person who needs to hear it. Three signals out of one sentence.

One rule, and it's the whole thing: the reframe has to be true. Flattery gets watched once. The truth gets saved.
